name: Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport
before:
The third Washington airport, and often the cheapest way into either city. It is in Anne Arundel County 14 km south of downtown Baltimore and 50 km north east of Washington DC, and it is one of Southwest Airlines' thirteen United States operating bases, which is what keeps fares competitive.

It carried 27.06 million passengers in 2024, a shade behind Dulles, having been the busiest of the three the year before. Either way, this is the one to price against when a client is flying into the capital.

There are three runways across 3,160 acres. Runway 28 is the main departure runway and 33L the main arrival, with Runway 10 carrying the highest instrument rating for poor visibility.

It opened as Friendship International and was renamed in 2005 after Thurgood Marshall, a Baltimore native and the first African American to sit on the United States Supreme Court. There is a proper aircraft viewing area at Friendship Park overlooking the landing runway.
after:
One of the three main airports for the Washington and Baltimore area, alongside Dulles and Reagan National. It is in Anne Arundel County, 14 km south of downtown Baltimore and 50 km north east of Washington DC, and is one of Southwest Airlines' 13 crew bases.

The airport handled about 25.2 million passengers in 2025, down about 7 per cent on 2024. That made it the second busiest of the three, behind Dulles and just ahead of Reagan National.

There are three runways. Plane spotters have a dedicated viewing area, the Dixon Aircraft Observation Area, with parking and a playground.

It opened as Friendship International. Since 2005 its name has also honoured Thurgood Marshall, a Baltimore native and the first African American to sit on the United States Supreme Court.

claims.claim: one of Southwest Airlines' 13 crew bases
claims.inAfter: is one of Southwest Airlines' 13 crew bases
claims.note: Was 'one of Southwest Airlines' thirteen United States operating bases'. Southwest's own careers page (read 23 Sep 2026, no date of its own) lists 13 crew bases, Baltimore (BWI) among them; 'crew bases' is Southwest's word. All 13 are in the US, so 'United States' is dropped as redundant. Southwest carried 71.28 per cent of BWI's passengers in 2025 (operator) and 73.48 per cent in the 12 months to June 2026 (BTS); not added, as the old text gave no share.

sources.quote: The airport serves as one of 13 U.S.-based operating bases for Southwest Airlines.

quote: Southwest currently has 13 Crew Bases:

Atlanta (ATL), Austin (AUS), Baltimore (BWI), Chicago (MDW), Dallas (DAL), Denver (DEN), Houston (HOU), Las Vegas (LAS), Los Angeles (LAX), Nashville (BNA), Oakland (OAK), Orlando (MCO), and Phoenix (PHX)

claims.claim: the airport describes itself as the lowest-cost airport for passengers in the National Capital Region
claims.note: Replaces 'often the cheapest way into either city', for which no fare comparison could be read: the Bureau of Transportation Statistics' fare page lists airport fare tables for the first quarter of 2026, but the links to them could not be read (bts.gov refused the link lister and WebFetch with 403; the browser copy holds the table titles only). The airport's own words are given as its claim, not as a fact.

sources.org: BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport (Maryland Aviation Administration, operator, bwiairport.com)
sources.quote: And as the lowest-cost airport for passengers in the National Capital Region, it consistently delivers value that travelers notice and airlines can build on.

claims.why: Held back in review (23 Sep): the airport's own marketing line, loose in meaning (it does not say whether it means fares, fees or parking), so it is not a like-for-like replacement for the old 'often the cheapest way in', which no fare source could confirm. Andy can add it as the airport's claim; the source stays listed here. Was to read: "The airport describes itself as the lowest-cost airport for passengers in the National Capital Region."
